key_insight: Compressing each weight matrix optimally on its own is not enough for good LLM compression. This paper shows that low-rank compression should be optimized across three levels—matrix, block, and whole model—because approximation errors interact through Transformer nonlinearities.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between per-matrix SVD truncation optimality and end-to-end model quality. Independently compressing matrices can look optimal locally but still produce compounded error and accuracy loss in the full Transformer.
method: Whiten each matrix and apply truncated SVD as the first-level (L1) compression step.
Perform block-level joint optimization (L2) to account for interactions among compressed matrices inside a Transformer block.
Extend optimization to the full model (L3) so the final compression objective reflects end-to-end performance rather than isolated matrix error.
impact: This provides a more reliable recipe for low-rank LLM compression, especially when preserving downstream accuracy matters more than local reconstruction error. For practitioners, it suggests better compression results with fewer surprises when deploying smaller, faster models.
visual_elements: A three-tier pyramid showing L1 matrix, L2 block, and L3 model optimization.
A side-by-side comparison of per-matrix SVD vs. joint optimization error propagation through a Transformer block.
A flowchart showing compression decisions moving from matrix-level to model-level.
Icons for matrices, Transformer blocks, and a full LLM to illustrate the hierarchy.
paper_title: Per-Matrix Optimality Is Not Enough: Three-Level Optimization for Low-Rank LLM Compression
paper_authors: Huicheng Zhang, Xiyao Feng, Ze-Tong Li, Chengkai Zhu, Xiao Shi
